articles.title: Physical distancing to prevent influenza-like illness on a college campus: The eX-FLU trial
articles.titleEn: Physical distancing to prevent influenza-like illness on a college campus: The eX-FLU trial
articles.abstract: Public health recommendations often advise people to isolate when infected with influenza-like illness (ILI) with the goal of promoting physical distancing and limiting face-to-face interactions when risk of transmission is highest. Because isolation may have negative consequences, it is important to carefully assess whether encouragement to physically distance actually prevents cases of ILI. College campuses can be especially vulnerable to outbreaks of ILI and are ideal environments for assessing the impact of encouragement-to-physically-distance interventions. The eX-FLU cluster-randomized trial followed 579 students on a college campus over a ten-week period during flu season to evaluate such an intervention. Students in the trial were randomized to receive the intervention—encouragement to isolate in their dorm room when symptomatic for ILI—or control. Evaluating the effect of this intervention is challenging because of dependence between students in the trial and an anticipated spillover effect of the intervention. Moreover, while the intervention was designed to affect both face-to-face interactions and ILI infections, the effect on ILI infections is of primary public health interest. In this paper, a randomization-based testing procedure is proposed to assess the intervention effect specifically on ILI infections in the presence of dependent data and spillover effects. The testing procedure is shown theoretically and empirically to control the type I error rate and have good statistical power to detect an intervention effect in trials similar to eX-FLU. When applied to the eX-FLU data, this testing procedure gives moderate evidence that the intervention reduced ILI infections.

articles.title: Elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
articles.titleEn: Elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
articles.abstract: Cells mechanically interact through the deformations they generate in their surrounding extracellular matrix. We present an analytical theory of the elastic interactions between cells that actively adapt their forces in response to local deformations of their environment. Cells are represented as localized contractile force generators, modeled as polarizable point force dipoles, whose adaptive forces are determined self-consistently with those of surrounding cells. Analysis of the associated elastic interaction energy identifies a generic short-ranged interaction arising from the mutual adaptation of cellular forces. This induced-dipole interaction is analogous to the van der Waals interaction between molecules and likewise is shown to be generally attractive for cells that enhance contractility in response to stretch. Furthermore, unlike the long-ranged elastic interaction between nonpolarizable force-dipoles, that peaks at intermediate matrix stiffness and then weakens as the matrix softens, the induced-dipole interaction strengthens monotonically as the matrix softens and can reverse the interaction from being repulsive at long cell distances to being attractive at short separations. Analytical calculations are presented to illustrate the mutual polarization of forces in pairs of interacting cells on a substrate. The identification of a generic, short-range cohesive elastic interaction between cells is important for understanding cell behavior at short separations and provides a physical mechanism driving cell accumulation on soft substrates.

articles.title: Emergent long-tailed dynamics in spin ice
articles.titleEn: Emergent long-tailed dynamics in spin ice
articles.abstract: In this study, we reveal long-tail dynamics spontaneously arising from a magnetic system. Specifically, we consider a classical spin system and demonstrate the emergence of a spin-ice physics when drive-induced heating is well suppressed. We show that at high driving frequencies, magnetic monopole excitations exhibit nonergodic stochastic dynamics characterized by power-law-distributed trapping times with long tails—a behavior that persists even in the absence of driving. At intermediate driving frequencies, the system eventually heats up to an infinite-temperature state. However, contrary to conventional wisdom of Floquet heating, the heating time in our model is extremely sensitive to different initial-state realizations and also follows a long-tailed power-law distribution, which arise specifically due to periodic driving. We show that an effective short-range attractive interaction between monopoles is responsible for the long-tailed distributions observed in both monopole and heating dynamics.

articles.title: Improving weather radar rainfall estimates by merging with commercial microwave link data: a fully reproducible, large-scale method intercomparison
articles.titleEn: Improving weather radar rainfall estimates by merging with commercial microwave link data: a fully reproducible, large-scale method intercomparison
articles.abstract: Accurate rainfall estimation is essential for hydrometeorological applications, but capturing the fine spatiotemporal variability of rainfall remains challenging. In this study, we assess the impact of merging commercial microwave link (CML) data with weather radar for quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) using two openly available datasets with contrasting observational densities. We compare multiple merging methods, including kriging with external drift (KED), and derive a block kriging interpolation method to account for the line-average nature of CMLs. The results show that merging CML data improves radar QPE, with reductions in mean absolute error (MAE) of up to 41 % for multiplicative merging and up to 38 % for KED, aligning well with similar studies using rain gauges. Performance depends on rainfall intensity, distance, and network density: in sparse networks, multiplicative methods yield the lowest RMSE and MAE, indicating that radar errors are dominated by scaling errors, though KED and additive methods maintain slightly higher spatial correlation (PCC) over distance. In dense networks, all methods perform comparably. Overall, additive methods perform best at capturing extremes. Despite accounting for line-averaging, block kriging performed similarly to point-based kriging. All merging methods reduced RMSE and MAE compared to unadjusted radar fields. The merging framework and intercomparison study are openly available, enabling reproducibility and further exploration by the scientific community.

articles.title: Unravelling groundwater's role in soil-plant-atmosphere continuum: integrated ecohydrological modelling approach using STEMMUS-SCOPE and MODFLOW 6
articles.titleEn: Unravelling groundwater's role in soil-plant-atmosphere continuum: integrated ecohydrological modelling approach using STEMMUS-SCOPE and MODFLOW 6
articles.abstract: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) models are commonly used to investigate various components' role(s) in ecosystem functioning. Yet, in most SPAC models, groundwater is ignored or at best represented in an over-simplified manner, leading to misunderstanding of its critical role in simulating soil-vegetation dynamics. This study investigates groundwater's role in SPAC processes, in particular, the impacts of groundwater component (mass and energy) on: (1) regulating the soil profile, in terms of moisture and temperature; (2) the dynamics of the unsaturated/saturated zones and their further impact on water fluxes; and (3) the carbon fluxes and vegetation physiological processes (i.e. root water uptake and photosynthesis reflected by fluorescence). To address this, an integrated ecohydrological modelling (IEM) framework is developed by coupling the STEMMUS-SCOPE SPAC model with the MODFLOW 6 integrated hydrological model. The standalone STEMMUS-SCOPE (ST-SC) and the coupled STEMMUS-SCOPE-MODFLOW 6 (ST-SC-MF6) models were applied over an 8-year period (1 April 2016–31 March 2024) to three sites in the Netherlands (Loobos, Cabauw and Veenkampen). Various essential variables, including soil moisture ( θ ), soil temperature ( T s ), groundwater level (GWL), groundwater temperature (GT), evapotranspiration (ET), gross primary productivity (GPP), net ecosystem exchange (NEE), and sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) were simulated and then compared to corresponding in-situ observations. Performance of both ST-SC and ST-SC-MF6 was evaluated using the Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) and the root mean square error (RMSE) metrics. Results indicated that the groundwater contribution is spatially and temporally variable. The ST-SC-MF6 model showed better agreement with observations than the ST-SC, improving the KGE values for: (a) θ (+0.29), T s (+0.19), and ET (+0.35) at Loobos, (b) θ (+0.30), T s (+0.14), NEE (+0.18), and SIF (+0.15) at Cabauw, and (c) θ (+0.21) and ET (+0.15) at Veenkampen. Notably, benefits of ST-SC-MF6 simulation were particularly prominent during both wet and dry periods, i.e. improving the representation of: (a) the θ dynamics during wet conditions, when hydraulic connectivity between the phreatic surface and the unsaturated zone is strong; (b) the root water uptake and carbon assimilation during dry periods, when shallow groundwater mitigated vegetative water stress; and (c) the T s dynamics during both wet and dry periods, influenced by both GT and GWL, and further propagated to other T s -dependent processes/variables such as canopy temperature. Overall, the proposed ST-SC-MF6 IEM helped to: (1) incorporate groundwater as a key component of the water, energy and carbon cycles; and (2) define the important role groundwater dynamics plays in the SPAC for deepening the understanding of ecosystem functioning.

articles.title: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
articles.titleEn: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
articles.abstract: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical composition, and internal morphology. Such particle-level details are not easily represented in large-scale atmospheric models. Existing parameterizations typically assume idealized particle geometries (e.g., homogeneous spheres or concentric core–shell spheres) and homogeneous mixing, which can yield biased predictions and provide no quantitative estimate of model-form uncertainty at the single-particle level. In this work, we present a probabilistic framework for predicting the optical properties of individual BC-containing particles using a hybrid Bayesian neural network (BNN) model trained on discrete dipole approximation (DDA) simulations. The hybrid BNN is a flexible combination of deterministic and Bayesian layers allowing for more realistic treatment of particle optical properties and quantification of uncertainty. The hybrid BNN model predicts extinction efficiency, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter and returns predictive uncertainty that can be decomposed into aleatoric (data-driven variability) and epistemic (uncertainty due to limited training coverage) components. We show that the hybrid BNN outperforms homogeneous-sphere and core–shell Mie approximations for calculating extinction and scattering-sensitive quantities ( Q ext , SSA and g ), while maintaining comparable accuracy for absorption-related metrics. We further demonstrate how epistemic uncertainty highlights under-sampled regions of particle parameter space, enabling targeted design of future DDA simulations that most effectively reduce model uncertainty. This uncertainty-aware surrogate provides a practical pathway for incorporating realistically complex particle morphologies into parameterizations of aerosol optical properties, which will ultimately improve the reliability of model-based assessments of BC impacts on the atmosphere.

articles.title: A simple weather generator that converts statistical information from downscaled global climate models to sequences of daily precipitation and temperature
articles.titleEn: A simple weather generator that converts statistical information from downscaled global climate models to sequences of daily precipitation and temperature
articles.abstract: A simple weather generator is presented that is designed to provide a link between downscaled precipitation or temperature statistics on the one hand, and impact models on the other. It generates time series of daily data that may be used as input for e.g. a hydrological model. It has a simple design which is described in this paper together with results from an evaluation against three rain gauge observations from Norway, Ghana and Romania respectively. It has also been tested for daily precipitation and temperatures from a number of sites representing different local climates in Ghana and Norway, and the results from these evaluations indicate that it reproduces the salient character in terms of the daily data and the observed climatology in different climatological settings. The simple design for precipitation, however, underestimate the duration of dry and wet spells for some sites to some degree. An assessment of the performance of daily temperature simulations from complimentary temperature-based weather generator for test sites in Ghana and Norway suggests that its output follows a similar statistical distribution as the original observations, however, there was some deviations particularly for the lowest temperatures. These two weather generators for daily precipitation and temperature respectively are part of the open-access R-package “esd” (version 1.11.30 or higher).

articles.title: Development and improvement of a nonhydrostatic spectral model using non-constant coefficient semi-implicit and vertically conservative semi-Lagrangian schemes
articles.titleEn: Development and improvement of a nonhydrostatic spectral model using non-constant coefficient semi-implicit and vertically conservative semi-Lagrangian schemes
articles.abstract: A two-dimensional x – z nonhydrostatic spectral model has been developed as a simpler framework for testing and improving numerical methods before they are applied to the corresponding global model. The model uses non-constant coefficient semi-implicit and vertically conservative semi-Lagrangian schemes and is computationally efficient by allowing for long timesteps in simulations. The model incorporates several improvements related to free-slip surface boundary conditions, prognostic variables in spectral space, and the semi-Lagrangian and semi-implicit schemes. These improvements enhance numerical stability, especially in cases with steep orography, and improve model results. The model was tested with various test cases (e.g., mountain wave test cases), confirming that a single recalculation of the non-constant coefficient linear terms is usually sufficient to stably solve the equations associated with the non-constant coefficient semi-implicit scheme, even in the cases with a steep mountain with an average slope of 45°. The model also ran stably even in the case of an extremely steep mountain with an average slope of 63.4° by performing several iterations using the preconditioned general conjugate residual method. In all these cases, good results were obtained with long timesteps.

articles.title: Belowground Productivity in Grasslands and Savannas Depends on Shifting Fire and Herbivory Regimes
articles.titleEn: Belowground Productivity in Grasslands and Savannas Depends on Shifting Fire and Herbivory Regimes
articles.abstract: In grasslands and savannas, most plant biomass and net primary productivity is belowground. How shifts in disturbance regimes, such as fire or large herbivore activity, impact belowground net primary productivity (BNPP) is unclear across climate‐driven productivity gradients. We tested the hypothesis that altered fire and herbivory regimes impact BNPP by changing the relative biomass of herbaceous and woody plants, which differ in their relative allocation to BNPP, and that climate constrains how much disturbance shifts this herbaceous–woody balance. We measured BNPP and aboveground vegetation across seven African and North American grasslands and savannas, with three long‐term fire manipulation levels (high frequency, intermediate frequency, and suppressed) and, at six sites, two long‐term herbivory levels (large herbivores excluded or open to large herbivores). Sites spanned an aridity index (mean annual precipitation [mm]/potential evapotranspiration [mm]) gradient—and associated woody thickening potential—from 0.21 to 0.71. BNPP increased with water availability. Fire and herbivory increased BNPP, with greater effects in wetter sites. In the wettest sites, BNPP gains under disturbance correlated with herbaceous biomass gains, as herbivory and frequent fire reduced woody plant cover relative to disturbance exclusion plots. BNPP responses were also predicted by root biomass, explaining why wetter sites and frequently disturbed plots within sites had higher BNPP. Climate determined how much the positive response of root biomass offset fire and grazing reductions in aboveground plant stocks, largely because water availability constrained the total aboveground plant biomass achieved without disturbance. Therefore, disturbances stimulated BNPP in wet savannas, largely by limiting woody thickening and promoting herbaceous growth with higher BNPP rates, whereas BNPP in drier and mesic sites tended to be resilient. Our findings show that belowground processes in grasslands and savannas fundamentally depend on disturbance regimes, climate‐driven productivity gradients, and their interactions, with important implications for understanding global carbon storage.

articles.title: Growing-season variability and environmental controls of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude terrestrial ecosystems
articles.titleEn: Growing-season variability and environmental controls of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude terrestrial ecosystems
articles.abstract: Rapid warming and accelerating ecological change across high-latitude (>66° N) terrestrial environments are reshaping greenhouse gas dynamics. However, spatiotemporal patterns and environmental drivers of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes in high-latitude ecosystems remain poorly understood. In this study we describe the seasonal and spatial variation in CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across key subarctic and boreal environmental gradients. A secondary aim is to examine the environmental drivers underlying these flux patterns. We measured fluxes during the snow-free season of 2024 and 2025 in northern Finland, starting early June (spring snowmelt) and ending late September (first snowfall). We conducted 1272 chamber measurements at 144 locations spanning eight high-latitude land cover classes: bare tundra, dwarf-shrub tundra, deciduous forest, evergreen forest, fen, bog, permafrost bog and tundra wetland. Bare tundra, dwarf-shrub tundra, deciduous forest and evergreen forest sites acted as net CH 4 sinks (mean flux of −0.16 to −0.05 mgm-2h-1, depending on land cover class) and as both N 2 O sources and sinks (−0.69 to 1.69 µgm-2h-1). Fen, bog, permafrost bog and tundra wetland sites were net CH 4 sources (mean flux of 0.93 to 27.81 mgm-2h-1) and net N 2 O sinks (−0.89 to −6.53 µgm-2h-1). Highest mean CH 4 fluxes occurred in fens (23.4 mgm-2h-1) and permafrost bogs (27.8 mgm-2h-1) which often coincided with substantial N 2 O sinks (mean flux of −6.53 in fens and −5.40 µgm-2h-1 in permafrost bogs). Seasonal trends were present for CH 4 but were land cover-dependent, with both sinks and sources typically peaking during July–August. Land cover class, soil temperature, and soil pH had the strongest effects on CH 4 fluxes while variation in N 2 O was best explained by soil pH and land cover class. However, a significant portion of the variability in N 2 O remained unexplained. These results demonstrate that strong spatial heterogeneity and pronounced seasonal dynamics during the snow-free period generate substantial variability in CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude ecosystems. Our findings suggest that monthly measurements of insitu gas fluxes and soil conditions in combination with accurate land cover mapping are essential for modelling and upscaling of GHG fluxes. This is especially important in high-latitude regions, where rapid warming is altering both ecosystem distributions and soil conditions with significant consequences for current and future GHG budgets.

Highest mean CH 4 fluxes occurred in fens (23.4 mgm-2h-1) and permafrost bogs (27.8 mgm-2h-1) which often coincided with substantial N 2 O sinks (mean flux of −6.53 in fens and −5.40 µgm-2h-1 in permafrost bogs). Seasonal trends were present for CH 4 but were land cover-dependent, with both sinks and sources typically peaking during July–August. Land cover class, soil temperature, and soil pH had the strongest effects on CH 4 fluxes while variation in N 2 O was best explained by soil pH and land cover class. However, a significant portion of the variability in N 2 O remained unexplained. These results demonstrate that strong spatial heterogeneity and pronounced seasonal dynamics during the snow-free period generate substantial variability in CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude ecosystems. Our findings suggest that monthly measurements of insitu gas fluxes and soil conditions in combination with accurate land cover mapping are essential for modelling and upscaling of GHG fluxes. This is especially important in high-latitude regions, where rapid warming is altering both ecosystem distributions and soil conditions with significant consequences for current and future GHG budgets.

articles.title: Spatial modelling of available aluminum in glacial till: informing a boreal forest soil carbon predictor
articles.titleEn: Spatial modelling of available aluminum in glacial till: informing a boreal forest soil carbon predictor
articles.abstract: Boreal forest soils store 30 % of global forest soil carbon, making them a crucial component of the carbon cycle. However, climate change at high latitudes is increasing temperatures and producing unpredictable precipitation patterns. Soil organic carbon (SOC) formation and stabilization is tied to precipitation patterns, thus climate change will inevitably influence the stability and longevity of boreal forest SOC. The current size and distribution of this reservoir is poorly understood, creating uncertainty under current and future climate scenarios. Previous research demonstrates mineral soil properties may be used to model boreal forest SOC accurately. The surface slope, depth of carbon enriched horizon, and climate characteristics are important parameters for modelling SOC and can generally be obtained or estimated via remote sensing. However, information about the availability of reactive aluminum – non-crystalline forms capable of interacting with organic matter to form stable carbon rich organometal complexes in mineral soils – is not widely available but is controlled by the weatherable aluminum in soil parent material. To bridge this gap, the Newfoundland and Labrador till geochemistry dataset was used here to map and model weatherable aluminum availability in glacial till across the island of Newfoundland as a function of geology and climate. The Random Forest Algorithm was employed to develop two models: one relying solely on the strength of geological and climatic variables, and the other drawing additionally on the spatial context of sample points. The first model performed well ( R 2 =0.60), however, adding a spatial component increased the performance of the second model ( R 2 =0.71). Bedrock type and proximity of the samples to certain units were indicated to be the strongest controls on aluminum availability, while environmental factors were less influential. Additionally, model uncertainty was calibrated empirically and mapped spatially, providing reliable and actionable information about the confidence of predictions over the study area. This project demonstrates the value of predictive geospatial modelling for till geochemistry mapping and delivers key aluminum availability predictions useful for future efforts in deriving SOC reservoir estimates across Newfoundland.

articles.title: Fresh tephra deposits from the Tajogaite Volcano boost thermophile proliferation and soil organic matter recovery
articles.titleEn: Fresh tephra deposits from the Tajogaite Volcano boost thermophile proliferation and soil organic matter recovery
articles.abstract: Tephra fallout deposition during volcanic eruptions overlays existing soils, profoundly altering their physical, chemical, and biological properties. This study investigates the impact of the newly deposited tephra blanket from the 2021 Tajogaite eruption (La Palma Island) on the molecular composition of soil organic matter and microbial diversity across different soil horizons. To our knowledge, this is the first study combining molecular pyrolysis, stable isotope analysis, and microbial sequencing to characterize the early biogeochemical transformation of soils affected by the Tajogaite eruption. A combination of 16S rRNA gene sequencing, pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), and elemental and isotope ratio mass spectrometry (EA/IRMS) was employed. Our results reveal marked differences in organic matter composition and microbial community structure across the tephra-covered soil profile, with patterns consistent with ongoing microbial transformation of organic carbon and nitrogen compounds. The soil horizon directly beneath the tephra layer (horizon O) displayed a higher abundance of labile organic compounds and a reduced presence of recalcitrant compounds compared to the deeper horizons (A and Bw). This pattern is strongly associated with the predominance of thermophilic bacteria, which contribute actively to the breakdown of complex organic materials such as lignin and hydrocarbons, and drive key biogeochemical processes including nitrogen and carbon cycling. The continuous geothermal influence of nearby fumaroles further supports the persistence and ecological success of thermophilic communities in these volcanic soils. These findings underscore the critical role of volcanic activity not only in reshaping soil structure but also in enhancing soil fertility and resilience through microbial-mediated processes. Understanding these dynamics is essential for soil management and ecosystem recovery strategies in volcanic regions, providing new insights into the long-term effects of tephra deposition on soil health and the carbon cycle.

articles.title: Morphological and phylogenic variability of red snow algae in snowpacks along a glacial valley in Alaska
articles.titleEn: Morphological and phylogenic variability of red snow algae in snowpacks along a glacial valley in Alaska
articles.abstract: Red snow blooms are visually similar but can be composed of different algal species and cell morphologies across sites, and the factors determining this spatial heterogeneity remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated spatial variation in community structure, algal cell size, and morphology along gradients of elevation across a glacier and its forefield in Alaska. Microscopic observations revealed that the ice-based snowpack was characterized by a greater proportion of spherical cells, whereas the soil-based snowpack was characterized by a greater proportion of non-spherical cells and larger spherical cells. Molecular analyses revealed that Sanguina predominated in the ice-based snowpack, while the relative abundance of other genera, including Chloromonas and Rosetta , were more abundant in the soil-based snowpack. Redundancy analysis showed that community structure was explained primarily by snow depth and elevation, whereas it was not significantly influenced by nutrient concentrations. Linear models further indicated that size of spherical cell decreased with elevation, and the abundance of non-spherical cells decreased with snow depth. These results suggest that while snowmelt-driven environmental gradients govern the overall morphological and phylogenetic variability of red snow algae, the underlying substrate (ice vs. soil) also contributes to community turnover, likely by providing access to distinct local cell reservoirs during melt progression. Collectively, these factors shape the taxonomic composition, morphotype assemblage, and spatial development of red snow blooms.

articles.title: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
articles.titleEn: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Since October 2024 the Météo-France operational convective scale model AROME-France has been using a 3DEnVar data assimilation (DA) scheme in order to improve the performance of severe weather prediction. This paper describes the configuration and evaluation of this 3DEnVar scheme. It summarizes the work carried out to configure this scheme in an operational context, with the inherent constraints of numerical robustness, compatible execution times, and of course correct performance of the forecasts produced. The adjustment of horizontal and vertical localization, inflation, hybridization, and the use of Incremental Analysis Updates (IAU) are studied in sensitivity experiments, and the impact on the spin-up is investigated. A configuration and its variation with IAU are thus defined and evaluated using different scores over a long period and on different severe meteorological situations (winter storms, fog, and High Precipitating Events): they largely outperform the operational 3D-Var. The version with IAU was implemented in the new operational version of the AROME-France assimilation system.

articles.title: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
articles.titleEn: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Quantitative analysis of sinkhole collapse hazard requires robust data in both space and time. It also needs a clear understanding of the factors and processes that contribute to observed sinkhole locations and dimensions. In many karst settings, these criteria are difficult to meet because of the millennia-long time scales over which sinkhole populations are generated and because of uncertainties around how geomorphological processes link to sinkhole dimensions. This study presents new data on the scaling and probability of sinkhole formation in evaporite karst on the eastern Dead Sea shore (Jordan). Several thousand cover collapse sinkholes have formed there in the past 40 years with minimal post-collapse modification. Genetic processes and timescales are thus well constrained. Utilising high-resolution satellite imagery (Pleiades, PNEO) from 2017–2024, integrated with prior datasets, we present an updated inventory of sinkhole occurrence, extent and dimensions through time over the period 1992–2024. The sinkhole number increased by 43 % from 1565 in 2018 to 2247 in 2024, reflecting a 22 % increase in the sinkhole-affected land area to ca. 179 610 m 2 (17.9 ha). Formation of new karst subsidence features has continued a northward and seaward advance, consistent with control from the decline of the Dead Sea base level. However, we also observed a localised revival in 2021–2022 of sinkhole formation in an area that had been apparently inactive since 2002. This combination of continued and renewed sinkhole formation poses significant challenges to agriculture, housing and infrastructure in the area. Sinkhole average diameters range from 1.1 to 72.9 m; their frequency follows a log-normal distribution, rather than a power-law. Representative annualised exceedance probabilities for formation of sinkholes with diameters greater than 5, 10 and 50 m are ca. 70 %, 30 % and 0.5 % respectively. Exceedance probabilities show slight dependence on sampling time interval and on the nature of near-surface materials in which sinkholes form. Given their log-normal size distribution, the Dead Sea cover collapse sinkholes are not scale-free; instead they are scale-bound by the evaporite karst system's geometrical and mechanical properties.

articles.title: Evaluating the performance of a numerical weather prediction model for precipitation and temperature in Luxembourg and the Greater Region: insights from WRF and WRFDA 3D-VAR
articles.titleEn: Evaluating the performance of a numerical weather prediction model for precipitation and temperature in Luxembourg and the Greater Region: insights from WRF and WRFDA 3D-VAR
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: We evaluate the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model, with and without WRFDA 3D-VAR data assimilation, for precipitation and temperature forecasts in Luxembourg and the Greater Region during the July 2021 flood event. Conventional observations, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) zenith total delay (ZTD) and their combination were assimilated 6-hourly over a month (20 June–20 July 2021), each cycle re-anchored to GFS so that all experiments share a common background. The climatological CV3 and an NMC-derived CV5 background error covariance were both tested, and forecasts verified against 264 independent surface stations in four countries. The covariance dominates the outcome. With CV3, assimilation raises rainfall frequency without improving discrimination and the equitable threat score falls from 0.383 to 0.337 at 0.1 mm per 6 h; with CV5 the same observations improve it, by +0.057 at 1 mm per 6 h. The gain is confined to low and moderate intensities, regionally uneven, and rests on an in-sample covariance. Adding ZTD to the conventional network gains +0.037, whereas adding conventional observations to ZTD gains nothing significant. For 2 m temperature, after height adjustment, no configuration is best. For this domain the background error covariance therefore matters more than the choice of observation type.

articles.title: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
articles.titleEn: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
articles.abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS 2 has long been considered a prime example of a Mott insulator driven by strong electron correlations. However, this view has been recently challenged by proposals which favor a band insulating state arising from interlayer dimerization. This ongoing debate opens a frontier in 1T-TaS 2 research focusing on stacking order, and raises a fundamental question with broad implications for two-dimensional materials: can electronic phases be engineered by actively tuning interlayer coupling? Here, using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that uniaxial strain drives 1T-TaS 2 from its insulating charge-density-wave phase into a stable metallic phase. This metallic phase, distinct from hydrostatic-pressure-induced or non-equilibrium hidden phases, emerges via a strain-induced rearrangement in the interlayer stacking of the Star-of-David charge order, effectively disrupting interlayer dimerization. Furthermore, the emergent metallic phase exhibits a significant quasiparticle mass renormalization, a hallmark of strong electron correlations, indicating its correlated nature and proximity to a Mott instability. This finding necessitates a re-evaluation of the interplay between structural and strong correlations in 1T-TaS 2 . The present results establish uniaxial strain as a powerful method for tuning the interlayer coupling, opening pathways for exploring quantum phases inaccessible under ambient conditions.

articles.title: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
articles.titleEn: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
articles.abstract: Early-life nutritional conditions may influence biological aging and age-related health, but the long-term associations of early exposure to sugar rationing remain unclear. Here we investigate the associations of early-life exposure to sugar rationing with biological aging and age-related diseases among 54,201 participants in the UK Biobank, taking advantage of the abrupt end of post-war sugar rationing as a natural experiment. Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life is associated with lower biological age acceleration, with stronger associations observed among participants with longer exposure durations. The association is more pronounced in females and remains consistent across strata of genetic susceptibility. Early-life exposure to sugar rationing is also associated with lower risks of age-related cataract and chronic kidney disease, but not with several other age-related diseases examined. Overall, these findings suggest that early-life exposure to a population-level nutritional policy is associated with biological aging and several age-related diseases in later life, highlighting the potential long-term relevance of early-life nutritional environments for healthy aging.

articles.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
articles.titleEn: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
articles.abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one ( n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart ( n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years ( n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [ n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [ n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

articles.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
articles.titleEn: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
articles.abstract: Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 (BM-MoS 2 ) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS 2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films enable a balance between the quality ( Q ) and optical confinement ( $$\varGamma$$ Γ ) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS 2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics.

articles.title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
articles.titleEn: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
articles.abstract: Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

articles.title: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li+ transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
articles.titleEn: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li+ transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
articles.abstract: Disordered rocksalt positive electrodes are promising candidates for high-energy batteries, yet their ion transport kinetics is constrained by an incomplete understanding of Li transport in disordered environments. Conventional percolation theory focuses on topological connectivity but often overlooks the critical role of the energy landscape. Here, leveraging actively fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potentials combined with experimental validation, we quantitatively resolve the interplay between Li percolation connectivity and the Li-site energy distribution. We reveal a trade-off whereby increasing cation disorder enhances topological connectivity but concurrently broadens the site energy distribution, inducing a rugged energy landscape that suppresses overall diffusion. To reconcile these conflicting factors, we construct a design map spanning the full Li–Mn–Ti–O composition space, establishing a Li-site energy rectified percolation metric that transforms their interaction into a quantifiable descriptor. This framework enables the identification of Li 1.3 Mn 0.4 Ti 0.3 O 2 , which delivers a specific capacity of 294 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we demonstrate that inducing a phase transition toward a partially disordered spinel-like state simultaneously enhances percolation connectivity and narrows the energy landscape, achieving a specific capacity of 316 mAh g −1 . This work provides insights into the ion transport mechanisms in disordered electrode materials and offers practical design principles for battery systems.

articles.title: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin-deficient neurons
articles.titleEn: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin-deficient neurons
articles.abstract: Neurons require mitochondrial bioenergetic flexibility to withstand chronic mitochondrial quality control failure, yet the compensatory safeguards that preserve mitochondrial functional output during neurodegenerative progression remain unclear. Here, using parkin- deficient fly models, we identify an early mitochondrial metabolic signature characterized by reduced pyruvate and increased glutamate and α-ketoglutarate. Substrate-specific mitochondrial respiration and ATP assays showed impaired pyruvate-supported bioenergetic capacity but preserved glutamate-supported bioenergetic capacity, supporting a transient glutamate-linked compensatory state before neurodegenerative deterioration. We identify neuronal TSPO upregulation as an adaptive compensatory mechanism that sustains glutamate-supported mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity under parkin -deficient conditions. In human iPSC-derived neurons, parkin deficiency was similarly associated with TSPO upregulation, and TSPO modulation altered neuronal vulnerability. TSPO induction was controlled by JNK-Jun/Nrf2 signaling, whose age-associated attenuation compromised compensation and accelerated neurodegeneration. Thus, loss of TSPO-dependent glutamate-linked bioenergetic compensation marks the transition from mitochondrial adaptation to neurodegenerative deterioration under parkin -deficient conditions.

articles.title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
articles.titleEn: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
articles.abstract: Parasympathetic nervous system activity, vital for restorative sleep, is influenced by vagal sensory afferents, but how these shape brain-body correlates of sleep remains open. Here we combined vagal sensory neuron (VSN) stimulation in the mouse with EEG/EMG, heart rate, brain-body temperature, noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) neuron population activity measures and in vitro synaptic physiology to investigate the effects of VSN activation on sleep-wake states. We show that chemogenetic VSN stimulation during the resting phase induced a non-rapid-eye-movement sleep (NREMS)-like state with enriched, but homeostatically regulated, low-frequency (0.75–4 Hz) EEG activity, yet suppressed REMS. Simultaneously, brain-body temperatures dropped while LC activity increased. The gradual recovery towards normal NREMS-REMS-cycles was accelerated by external warming, identifying cooling as key contributing factor. We conclude that VSN activation can promote brain-body correlates as a continuum of normal NREMS while engaging wake-promoting forebrain neuromodulation, revealing a coexistence of classically incompatible sleep- and wake-associated signatures.

articles.title: Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
articles.titleEn: Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
articles.abstract: Cholesterol crystallization within phospholipid bilayers necessarily remodels the surrounding membrane, creating dynamic feedback between growing crystallites and locally changing membrane. Using fluorescence microscopy, we show that lipid-coated, cholesterol-rich crystallites self-propel on the bilayer surface along directional trajectories, including circular, unidirectional, and reciprocating motion. We hypothesize that crystallite motilities arise from local cholesterol depletion in the underlying bilayer, generating gradients in composition, rigidity, and thus adhesion, which induce directional forces analogous to those involved in haptotaxis and/or durotaxis. Fluorescence lifetime imaging with a mechanosensitive probe reveals time-resolved changes in membrane packing, consistent with this mechanism. Single particle tracking and mathematical modeling support the mechanical plausibility of a working model in which crystallization-induced cholesterol redistribution may generate dynamic rigidity gradients at crystallite–membrane interface. Tuning membrane states yields a quantitative operating map that relates composition to motility, providing model-dependent design guidance for controlling cholesterol crystallite transport on lipid interfaces.

articles.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
articles.titleEn: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
articles.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
articles.titleEn: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
articles.abstract: Large-scale circulation waviness shapes day-to-day weather and extremes. During 1989 to 2011, Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes experienced a pronounced increase in wintertime waviness, coinciding with rapid Arctic warming and more frequent cold-air outbreaks. While Arctic amplification was hypothesized to cause this trend via jet weakening, subsequent studies have failed to support this mechanism, leaving the origin unresolved. Here, using large-ensemble simulations, statistical analyses, and dynamical diagnostics, we demonstrate that variability in sea surface temperature and sea ice accounts for approximately half (48.7 to 63.3%) of the observed increase. A positive phase shift of the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) is the prominent driver, enhancing waviness across northern Eurasia, the northwest Pacific, and the North Atlantic. A concurrent negative Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation shift partially offsets the AMO-driven anomalies in the northwest Pacific. Projections indicate that internal variability will outweigh model differences as the main source of near-term uncertainty. These results refine attribution of recent winter waviness changes and identify an AMO-linked source of predictability for long-term shifts in midlatitude extremes.

articles.title: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars
articles.titleEn: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars
articles.abstract: High-resolution x-ray spectroscopy of classical T Tauri stars (CTTs) reveals a soft x-ray excess, low electron density, and accretion rate inferred from helium-like oxygen (O VII). Accretion shock models have been widely studied via numerical simulations and can reproduce observations with appropriate accretion stream structures. Within the standard accretion shock framework, we propose a distinct physical model involving energy exchange between postshock hot plasma and cold infalling material during reverse shock propagation into the accretion stream. Incorporating charge exchange processes, the electron density derived from the O VII triplet shows excellent agreement with helium-like neon diagnostics and standard accretion shock model predictions. The mass accretion rate inferred from O VII emission also becomes consistent with optical results. Complementing our theoretical work, we conducted a laboratory simulation of CTT accretion shocks supported by hydrodynamic similarity principles. Time-integrated x-ray self-emission and temporal optical shadowgraphy reveal the dynamic formation of two dense clumps, the “core” and “shell,” which morphologically resemble hydrodynamic oscillations driven by heating/cooling instabilities in CTT accretion shocks. The core is a standing shock formed by a preheated low-density plasma flow impinging on a carbon-hydrogen foil, while the shell is shocked aluminum plasma (the reverse shock) arising from interactions between accumulated aluminum plasma and its following flow. High-resolution experimental spectra confirm that charge exchange occurs in the shocked x-ray–emitting region. Our results demonstrate that dynamic interactions between postshock and infalling material, mediated by charge exchange cooling, is the reason for the low O VII density problem in CTTs.

articles.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring
articles.titleEn: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring
articles.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today’s wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)–powered ring for all-optical sensing of dermal activity (ODA), using light rather than electrodes to track sweat gland activation, thereby enhancing durability and comfort. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

articles.title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
articles.titleEn: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
articles.abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

articles.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
articles.titleEn: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
articles.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

articles.title: Physics-informed and data-efficient machine learning for storm surge forecasting during typhoons
articles.titleEn: Physics-informed and data-efficient machine learning for storm surge forecasting during typhoons
articles.abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting storm surges during tropical cyclones, which is crucial in reducing coastal damages. We develop a physics-informed and data-efficient model, a storm surge neural network (SSNN), that embeds shallow water equations into a machine learning (ML) framework with a specifically designed piecewise loss function to effectively incorporate physical constraints. The SSNN is iteratively trained to make rolling forecast and can produce more accurate forecasts than a standard data-driven model even with a smaller size of training data. The improvement in the performance by the SSNN model is evident, particularly in coastal areas with varying strong winds. This is especially true for forecasts beyond 16 hours, where the data-driven model struggles to provide accurate predictions. Combining physics with ML could offer a promising way to improve storm surge forecasting and support coastal hazard preparedness.

articles.title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
articles.titleEn: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
articles.abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

articles.title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
articles.titleEn: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
articles.abstract: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH 3 ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. articles.title: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
articles.titleEn: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
articles.abstract: Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells have been paradoxically implicated in tissue repair and fibrosis. However, when and how they modulate fibrogenesis in distinct tissue environments remain unclear. Using the carbon tetrachloride model of liver injury in major histocompatibility complex–related protein 1 (MR1)– and MAIT cell–sufficient and –deficient mice, we identify MAIT cells as early drivers of fibrogenesis. MAIT cells exacerbated hepatocellular injury, myofibroblast activation, and matrix deposition during fibrosis initiation, coinciding with rapid polarization toward a MAIT17 phenotype and induction of a profibrotic transcriptional program. Despite acquiring an exhaustion-associated phenotype, MAIT cells retained their effector functions. Mechanistically, MAIT cells limited hepatic regulatory T (T reg ) cell accumulation, accompanied by reduced Ki-67 and CXCR3 levels in the latter population. Furthermore, in vivo T reg cell inactivation abrogated MAIT cell–dependent differences in fibrosis severity. Together, these findings identify MAIT cells as early orchestrators of fibrogenesis and reveal a previously unappreciated MAIT-T reg axis that can be therapeutically targeted in the early stages of fibrotic diseases.

articles.title: Improving Global Simulation of Irrigation Within the Land Information System
articles.titleEn: Improving Global Simulation of Irrigation Within the Land Information System
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Irrigated agriculture increases evapotranspiration and near surface humidity, decreases air and ground temperatures, augments downwind precipitation, enhances recharge, and depletes surface water and/or groundwater resources. However, model developers have been slow to incorporate irrigation. Using the latest satellite‐based land cover and irrigation data sets and innovative modeling approaches, we developed a scheme for simulating irrigation in the Land Information System (LIS). We reconciled global and national irrigation, land cover, and crop class databases in an effort to (a) distinguish irrigated and rainfed agriculture, (b) approximate fractional crop cover in each model grid pixel, and (c) apply the most likely irrigation method based on the crop class and country or state level information on the relative usage of sprinkler, furrow, paddy, and drip irrigation. Each irrigation method is represented by a separate algorithm. We used agricultural water withdrawal data, as available, for calibration and evaluation. The results compare favorably with available observational and reported data in terms of patterns. The simulated mean annual global irrigation rate, 2,765 km 3 /yr, is on par with an observational estimate (2,500 km 3 /yr) and other irrigation simulating models (mean 2,700 km 3 /yr). Over the contiguous U.S., based on county level reported irrigation water usage data, the new scheme had a root mean square error of 0.22 km 3 while correctly simulating the occurrence of irrigation in 3,053 of 3,220 irrigated counties, compared with 0.24 km 3 /yr and 2,334 counties for LIS's original scheme. Irrigation is estimated to increase global evapotranspiration by 1,700 km 3 /yr (2.4%), similar to a recent independent estimate.

articles.title: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
articles.titleEn: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
articles.abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrated that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)–compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observed antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial lanthanum (La)–doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and showed that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

articles.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
articles.titleEn: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
articles.abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

articles.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
articles.titleEn: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
articles.abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

articles.title: Tracking danger on the peaks
articles.titleEn: Tracking danger on the peaks
articles.abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

articles.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
articles.titleEn: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
articles.abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

articles.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
articles.titleEn: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

articles.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
articles.titleEn: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
articles.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

articles.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
articles.titleEn: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
articles.abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

articles.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak
articles.titleEn: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak
articles.abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

articles.title: Quantifying the hierarchical topological decay of fluid knots
articles.titleEn: Quantifying the hierarchical topological decay of fluid knots
articles.abstract: In this paper we analyze the hierarchical topological cascade of knotted and linked filaments associated with the natural decay of superfluid vortex tangles. This is done by using an algebraic reformulation of knot polynomial invariants to quantify the topological states of the cascade process. By interpreting the evolutionary paths associated with vortex knot dynamics as geodesic flows in an appropriate knot polynomial space defined by adapted Jones polynomials [X. Liu, R. L. Ricca, J. Phys. A Math. Theor. 45 , 205501 (2012).], we introduce an entanglement index to quantify the probability density of occurrence of each topological state. By this method we analyze all prime knots, links, and composites up to 8 crossings, and show that this measure detects accurately the decreasing topological complexity observed in simulations and laboratory experiments. By a comparative analysis carried out with data based on an alternative measure (complexity degree), we show that this entanglement index proves to be a more robust and reliable quantifier. The theoretical framework proposed here can be applied to other types of physical systems, where networks of filamentary structures are subject to continuous topological change and reorganization.
