articles.title: Diffusional depth profiling using electrochemiluminescence microscopy
articles.titleEn: Diffusional depth profiling using electrochemiluminescence microscopy
articles.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) microscopy has emerged as a powerful 2D imaging technique with exceptional spatial resolution, enabling visualization of biological entities, nanomaterials, and multiphase systems. Conventional ECL experiments rely on coreactant concentrations in large excess of the luminophore to generate a bright signal in the vicinity of the electrode. While effective for surface interrogation, this confinement limits resolution in the z-dimension, making 3D imaging challenging. Here, we show that introducing an excess of luminophore enables access to 3D information through diffusion of the emission layer away from the electrode. By tuning the concentration ratio of tris(2,2’-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) ([Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ) to tri-n-propylamine (TPrA), we control emission layer diffusivity. Initially, ECL arises from heterogeneous oxidation of both species at the electrode. As TPrA is depleted, the mechanism shifts to chemiluminescence, where [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 3+ oxidizes TPrA, generating a diffusing emissive layer that extends in the z-direction over time. Simulations and scanning electrochemical microscopy capture these diffusion profiles and highlight the role of concentration ratios. We apply this “diffusional depth profiling” to spirulina algae and spheroid cell models, insulating bodies that block light coming from the evolving emissive layer, revealing 3D morphology. This work uncovers the important influence of time and concentration on ECL emission layer expansion for depth profiling micro-to-mesoscale entities across biology and materials science.

articles.title: The p38α MAPK–MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression
articles.titleEn: The p38α MAPK–MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression
articles.abstract: Nuclear F-actin facilitates DNA damage repair and contributes to cancer chemoresistance. However, the regulatory mechanisms controlling its dynamic polymerization in response to genotoxic stress remain poorly defined. A major barrier in nuclear actin research is the lack of tools for precise, high-throughput analysis. To systematically investigate nuclear F-actin assembly in DNA damage response, we developed a deep learning pipeline, named nFANet, for high-throughput detection and analysis of nuclear F-actin. Here, using ovarian cancer—a malignancy where chemoresistance is a major clinical obstacle—as a model, we showed that platinum-based chemotherapy robustly induces nuclear F-actin assembly. A subsequent kinome screening, in combination with the application of nFANet, identified the kinase p38α MAPK as a critical upstream regulator of platinum-induced nuclear F-actin assembly. Mechanistically, the p38α MAPK–MK2 signaling pathway promotes formin-mediated nuclear F-actin assembly in response to chemotherapy. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockout of the p38α MAPK–MK2 pathway sensitized ovarian cancer cells to platinum-based therapy. Our work uncovers a key mechanism governing nuclear actin remodeling under genotoxic stress and lays the foundation for identifying a patient subgroup likely to benefit from therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

articles.title: Irrigation Water Withdrawals for Fruits, Vegetables, and Tree Nuts in the Continental United States From 2008 to 2020
articles.titleEn: Irrigation Water Withdrawals for Fruits, Vegetables, and Tree Nuts in the Continental United States From 2008 to 2020
articles.abstract: Irrigation represents a major use of water in the United States, yet irrigation water withdrawals are poorly characterized for individual crops. This study estimates irrigation water withdrawals for fruits, vegetables, and tree nut crops grown in the United States. We quantify surface water withdrawals, groundwater withdrawals, and nonrenewable groundwater depletion (GWD) for 65 crops at the county scale across the continental United States from 2008 to 2020. Estimates are generated using a physical irrigation model that disaggregates aggregate irrigation withdrawals for crop categories into individual crops based on crop‐specific irrigated area and relative evapotranspiration rates derived from crop coefficients. Over the study period, irrigation water use for specialty crops was highly concentrated, with only a handful of crops accounting for the majority of withdrawals within most counties. Almonds, grapes, and walnuts account for nearly 50% of all GWD across specialty crops. 49 out of 65 produce crops (75%) rely on groundwater where at least half of the withdrawals are depletionary, raising sustainability concerns. Crop‐level disaggregation also revealed structural differences between perennial and annual crops. This study presents the first national‐scale, crop‐specific assessment of irrigation water withdrawals for fruits, vegetables, and tree nuts by water source, county, and year. Because crop‐specific ground‐truth irrigation data are unavailable, estimates should be interpreted as relative, best‐available estimates rather than direct measurements; sources of uncertainty are discussed and, where possible, quantified. articles.title: Reply to Comment on “Deep Learning Identification of the Governing Equation for Water Flow in Heterogeneous Soils From Data” by Lee et al.
articles.titleEn: Reply to Comment on “Deep Learning Identification of the Governing Equation for Water Flow in Heterogeneous Soils From Data” by Lee et al.
articles.abstract: We appreciate Lee et al.’s interest in our article on identifying governing equations for water flow in heterogeneous soils. For their first concern regarding the role of deep learning in equation discovery, we clarify the synergy between sparse regression and deep learning. Sparse regression identifies the equation structure, while deep learning provides fine‐grained estimates of the nonlinear coefficient functions that depend on water content and depth. For their second concern regarding regularization sensitivity, we explain why their alternative ridge formulation is not equivalent to the complete grouped identification procedure of Extended‐DeepGS. Ridge regularization is integral to this solver: it stabilizes coefficient estimates when columns of the candidate library are correlated. Additional analyses show that the method consistently recovers the reference equation structure as the ridge parameter varies by nearly three orders of magnitude. More broadly, we hope this exchange promotes transparent and interpretable approaches to data‐driven equation discovery in hydrology.

articles.title: Assessing Temporal Consistency in Satellite‐Based and Modeled Soil Moisture Products and Its Implications for Trend Detection and Drought Monitoring
articles.titleEn: Assessing Temporal Consistency in Satellite‐Based and Modeled Soil Moisture Products and Its Implications for Trend Detection and Drought Monitoring
articles.abstract: Soil moisture is a critical state variable governing land‐atmosphere feedbacks, carbon cycling, and hydrological processes, yet existing long‐term data sets remain constrained by limitations in temporal continuity and cross‐sensor consistency. Individual remote sensing records are too short to resolve multi‐decadal trends; land surface model outputs are limited by deficiencies in process representations and parameterization choices; and merged satellite records risk introducing non‐physical artifacts through sensor transitions and algorithmic merging. In this study, we systematically evaluate the temporal consistency and reliability of three widely used soil moisture data sets: the European Space Agency Climate Change Initiative gap‐filled merged observational product (ESA CCI), the land data assimilation‐based NASA HydroGlobe, and the L‐band passive microwave Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) record. We assess their suitability for trend detection, uncertainty characterization, and extreme event monitoring. Our analysis reveals noticeable heterogeneity in temporal variability, signal‐to‐noise ratios, and probability distributions within the ESA CCI merged product that cannot be fully explained by precipitation variability. We further identify systematic regional discrepancies in seasonal soil moisture trends across all three products, persisting even in regions where internal product inconsistencies are not expected. Drought sensitivity evaluation across the Contiguous United States demonstrates that NASA HydroGlobe exhibits good skill in capturing drought anomalies, consistently outperforming the other data sets across most drought severity categories. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of carefully accounting for product‐specific assumptions, data lineage, and algorithmic choices when conducting decadal‐scale hydrological and climate analyses, and highlight the need for more robust benchmarking frameworks for long‐term soil moisture records.

articles.title: Development Length and Transport Regimes of Buoyant Plastics in Open‐Channel Flows
articles.titleEn: Development Length and Transport Regimes of Buoyant Plastics in Open‐Channel Flows
articles.abstract: Recent studies suggest that the vertical distribution of positively buoyant plastic particles in turbulent open‐channel flows can be described by a modified Rouse profile. However, experimental evidence also indicates that floating particles often remain confined to the air–water interface due to surface tension, with limited vertical exchange. These observations suggest a tension in the interpretation of Rouse‐type profiles for positively buoyant plastics. To address this, we first derive an expression for a particle development length, defined as the streamwise distance required for particles to interact with the controlling boundary. This provides a diagnostic measure of whether particles have had sufficient opportunity to interact with the boundary, and suggests that previous experimental studies may have operated within a developing regime. Second, we develop a regime map that integrates free‐surface detachment and bed‐entrainment processes within the Rouse framework, providing a predictive description of the dominant transport regimes for both positively and negatively buoyant plastics. Together, these results highlight the critical role of boundary interactions in plastic transport and support improved prediction of plastic pollution dynamics in riverine environments.

articles.title: Comment on “Deep Learning Identification of the Governing Equation for Water Flow in Heterogeneous Soils From Data” by Song et al.
articles.titleEn: Comment on “Deep Learning Identification of the Governing Equation for Water Flow in Heterogeneous Soils From Data” by Song et al.
articles.abstract: This comment examines the Extended‐DeepGS framework proposed by Song et al. (2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2024wr037786 ) to identify governing equations for soil moisture dynamics in heterogeneous soils. Extended‐DeepGS combines neural‐network based reconstruction and automatic differentiation with sparse regression. We clarify that these components have different but complementary roles. The neural network reconstructs the soil moisture field, reduces noise, interpolates between observations, and estimates derivatives. Sparse regression identifies the structure of the governing equation. We also examine how sensitive the identified partial differential equation (PDE) is to the ridge‐regularization parameter . A pseudo‐inverse ridge‐regression analysis of the sandy loam, loam, and silt loam cases shows that changing can change the selected active terms and the resulting equation structure. This result also applies to the value reported in Song et al. (2022, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022wr031926 ). An Extended‐DeepGS comparison for the loam case shows a similar pattern. Under the noise‐free conditions examined here, the pseudo‐inverse method recovered a low‐order PDE structure similar to that obtained with Extended‐DeepGS while requiring much less computation. These findings show the importance of separating the roles of deep learning and sparse regression. They also highlight the need to clearly report how is chosen and to test the stability of the identified equation structure.

articles.title: aiLand v1: physics-based land surface emulator with observational fine-tuning
articles.titleEn: aiLand v1: physics-based land surface emulator with observational fine-tuning
articles.abstract: A stand-alone emulator of ECMWF's land surface scheme (ecLand) has been developed. This emulator, aiLand, uses a multi-layer perceptron architecture, chosen for its balance of accuracy and efficiency and for its differentiability, which is crucial for integration into data assimilation and parameter estimation systems. In this study, we introduce a two-stage learning framework that leverages both synthetic land surface model simulations and real-world observations. We first pretrain the surrogate on extensive ecLand outputs to capture the core dynamical behaviour of key land surface states, evaluating its accuracy, long-term stability, and transferability across variables, depths, and climates. We then fine-tune the pretrained model on in situ eddy-covariance flux observations for selected diagnostic variables, validating against independent flux-tower sites. The pretrained emulator reproduces ecLand's prognostic soil state with a 90 d RMSE of 1.19 K for surface soil temperature and 0.014 m 3 m −3 for surface soil moisture, and remains stable over continuous 4-year autoregressive integrations. A single globally trained model outperforms regime-specialist baselines in cross-regime transfer, with residual errors concentrating in snow-insulated cold regimes where an insulating snowpack decouples the soil from atmospheric forcing. Fine-tuning on FLUXNET observations reduces latent heat flux RMSE by 30 % and sensible heat flux by 20 % at validation sites, while preserving prognostic state integrity and improving the physical consistency of the surface energy budget: per-site Bowen ratio error drops by 42% and energy balance closure residuals fall from 13.4 to 3 W m −2 and below. These results demonstrate that combining physics-based pretraining with observation-based fine-tuning provides a flexible pathway for building accurate, stable, and differentiable land surface emulators suitable for data assimilation and coupled modelling applications.

articles.title: BOWTIE: ship-based measurements of atmosphere and ocean within the moist tropical Atlantic
articles.titleEn: BOWTIE: ship-based measurements of atmosphere and ocean within the moist tropical Atlantic
articles.abstract: As part of BOWTIE (German: Beobachtung von Ozean und Wolken – Das Trans ITCZ Experiment), the German research vessel FS Meteor navigated the moist tropics of the Atlantic Ocean for 40 d in summer 2024, with an east-west trajectory. The journey started in the port of Mindelo, Cape Verde, on 16 August, and finished in the port of Bridgetown, Barbados, on 24 September. The objective was to measure properties of the atmosphere, upper ocean, and air-sea interface within the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), under a variety of wind, convection, and sea surface temperature regimes. Using a set of 29 instruments/platforms, BOWTIE sampled the near-surface conditions of the atmosphere and ocean with high temporal resolution. This included continuous measurements of: the 2D wind field within the lowest 2 km of the atmosphere, near-surface ocean currents, cloud and precipitation properties. Profiles of the ocean state and atmospheric thermodynamics and kinematics were obtained both continuously and at discrete intervals. Furthermore, biochemical properties of the upper ocean were sampled during dedicated stations. Complementing BOWTIE observations, FS Meteor hosted further dedicated field campaigns for 3D cloud and precipitation properties, as well as intensive measurements of the atmospheric boundary layer. This manuscript provides an overview of the extensive instrumentation and data collected during BOWTIE. In addition, it addresses two key aspects based on these observations. First, it examines the range and uncertainties of selected quantities measured by multiple instruments, including column-integrated water vapor, rain detection, surface ocean currents, and sea surface temperature. Second, it illustrates the diversity of sampled weather regimes through two representative cases: calm doldrum conditions and a gusty, precipitating convective state. The links and DOIs of the data sets presented in this study are listed in the code and data availability section.

articles.title: Future projections of compound events around the Main Hawaiian Islands
articles.titleEn: Future projections of compound events around the Main Hawaiian Islands
articles.abstract: The consequences of overlapping environmental stressors – referred to as compound events – may be more harmful to marine ecosystems than as individual stressors. Using recently conducted submesoscale-permitting future projections for the Main Hawaiian Islands, we present the first assessment of future compound events for Hawaiian waters. Our analysis focuses on surface and sub-surface heat-stress, ocean acidification, and low-oxygen events and is based on three different greenhouse gas emission scenarios. We show that a large fraction of ocean around Hawai'i will be subject to compound events in the near future. However, the projected event characteristics such as duration and intensity vary substantially across the region suggesting that potential ecosystem impacts may differ over short distances. Our results reveal that these spatial differences are mainly driven by considerably different magnitudes of natural variability in ocean physics and chemistry across the domain driven by mesoscale processes, while anthropogenic trends exhibit only minor spatial differences. Our analysis demonstrates that small-scale tidal variability can significantly mitigate compound events in near-shore regions, including some designated Marine Protected Areas. Overall, our findings highlight the need for high-resolution numerical models as well as for an extended observation network for robust future projections of local extreme events.

articles.title: Predicting slope instabilities in Salvador, Brazil, using machine learning and georeferenced data
articles.titleEn: Predicting slope instabilities in Salvador, Brazil, using machine learning and georeferenced data
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Municipalities worldwide struggle with slope instability, a particularly pressing issue in cities such as Salvador, Brazil, where rugged terrain, escarpments, and complex geology create a high risk of instability. The complexity of the problem is evident in the variability of terrain properties, the bedrock’s inherited structural features, and anthropogenic action. This range of variables makes it well-suited to machine learning (ML) approaches for instability prediction. Although ML has experienced an impressive recent boost, only a few cases have applied ML to real-world instability events. In this paper, a data bank of hydromechanical properties of soils is used in conjunction with a digital terrain model (DTM) and different geo-referenced information, including rainfall, vegetation coverage, geological structures, sewage collection/treatment status, and residential density, to predict the occurrence of soil mass movements and related emergency calls to the municipality from the population living in risk areas. 13 522 emergency calls were considered during the period from 2020 to 2025. Excellent predictive performance, with an R 2 ≈ 0.98 consistently across both the validation and testing phases, was obtained in this original study. This strong result underscores the viability of machine learning as a powerful tool for this kind of problem, particularly within municipal warning systems.

articles.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
articles.titleEn: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
articles.abstract: A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image 1–4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features 3,5–7 , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source 8,9 . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

articles.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
articles.titleEn: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
articles.abstract: In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status 1 . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

articles.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
articles.titleEn: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz
articles.abstract: Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene 1 , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats 2–7 , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

articles.titleEn: State of Wildfires 2025–2026
articles.abstract: The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. The State of Wildfires project systematically tracks global and regional fire activity, analyses the causes of prominent extreme wildfire events for three focal regions, and projects the likelihood of similar events under future climate scenarios. During the March 2025–February 2026 fire season, global burned area (BA) was 18 % below the 2002–2024 average and global fire carbon (C) emissions were also 20 %–31 % below average, making it one of the lowest years on record. Yet this globally low fire year still produced widespread regional impacts. Canada experienced a third consecutive extreme fire year, with national fire C emissions at nearly triple the average since 2002, 70 000 evacuations, and reported direct losses of USD 360 million. In the Midwestern Canadian Shield Forests, the epicentre of Canada's anomalous season, we find that anthropogenic climate change has nearly doubled (likely synthesis range 0.33–44.9, median 1.85) the likelihood of extreme fire weather in this region and made the observed BA around 10 times more likely during July–August 2025. BA extent in the region is found to be 9 times greater. Many parts of Europe also experienced record or high-ranking BA and fire C emissions, including in Spain, Portugal, and the UK, and a record USD 4.11 billion of physical assets were exposed to fire across the continent. Direct fatalities occurred in Türkiye (17), Spain (8), Portugal (6), Cyprus (2), Greece (1) and France (1), and evacuations in Türkiye, Spain, and Greece totalled over 110 000. In the Northwest Iberian Peninsula, we find that extreme fire weather over August 2025 was around 3 times (virtually certain modelled range 0.14–657, median 3.63) more likely due to climate change. Under a high-emissions scenario (SSP3-7.0), fires of the same return interval are likely to burn about 78 % more area by the end of the century, with some projections within the same scenario suggesting increases of around sevenfold. In Chile and northwest Argentina, January–February 2026 fires caused 23 fatalities, displaced 55 000 people and threatened a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the Chilean Temperate Forests and Matorral, the epicentre, we find that BA was around two times larger due to anthropogenic climate change. Across all focal regions in this report, the conditions for extreme fire developed gradually through months of precipitation deficits, cumulative drying and, in the case of Northwest Iberia, antecedent fuel accumulation aided by preceding wet periods. Continued climate change is expected to intensify these hydroclimatic extremes. However, comparison of SSP3-7.0 with SSP5-8.5 suggests that projected end-of-century extreme BA events in our focal regions are 4 %–23 % smaller than under the very high-emissions futures that were once considered plausible.. Meeting the Paris targets (SSP1-2.6) would further reduce BA during these events by 5 %–36 % across our focal regions. By integrating expertise from across the wildfire community with state-of-the-art observations, data, and modelling, this annual report advances understanding of regional wildfire extremes and their drivers, providing evidence to inform policy, preparedness, mitigation, adaptation, and broader societal benefit. Fifteen new and updated datasets created in this report are available from the State of Wildfires Project's Zenodo community (https://zenodo.org/communities/stateofwildfiresproject/, last access: 23 October 2026).

articles.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
articles.titleEn: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
articles.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity 1–5 . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells) 6 . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1 ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 ( Rgs2 ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

articles.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
articles.titleEn: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
articles.abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm 1,2 . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated 3–13 . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β- N -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations 14 of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization 4,5,7,9,15 and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

articles.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
articles.titleEn: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
articles.abstract: Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

articles.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
articles.titleEn: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
articles.abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

articles.title: Chromatin dynamics secondary to dexamethasone exposure identifies 67 genes linked to elevated IOP and primary open-angle glaucoma
articles.titleEn: Chromatin dynamics secondary to dexamethasone exposure identifies 67 genes linked to elevated IOP and primary open-angle glaucoma
articles.abstract: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a chronic neurodegenerative disorder, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) represents its only modifiable risk factor. We modeled increased IOP by treating three primary human trabecular meshwork cell strains with dexamethasone and generated a high-resolution map of promoter-centered chromatin contacts and regulatory modules. We identify dynamic changes in chromatin compartments and looping, cis-regulatory elements, and transcription factor hubs corresponding to altered expression profile. By integrating Genomewide association studies associated variants with dexamethasone induced chromatin landscape, we ascertain 29 target genes linked to 23 lead IOP variants and 57 genes for 46 POAG variants, with 19 shared between the two. Pathway analysis of 67 IOP- and POAG-associated genes reveals enrichment in vesicle transport, TLR, MAPK, and hippo-YAP signaling pathways. We also uncover transcriptional regulatory role of 103 noncoding lead variants. Our studies provide a mechanistic framework of genetic complexity accompanying steroid-induced IOP and related POAG pathology.

articles.title: Beyond Precipitation Deficit: Driver‐Based Classification of Hydrological Droughts in an Alpine Basin
articles.titleEn: Beyond Precipitation Deficit: Driver‐Based Classification of Hydrological Droughts in an Alpine Basin
articles.abstract: Hydrological droughts in mountain basins can arise from different combinations of precipitation deficits, snow accumulation and melt anomalies, and seasonal storage conditions. Here, we develop a deterministic, locally calibrated framework to classify recurrent hydro‐meteorological pathways associated with streamflow drought onset in the Upper Adige basin, Italy. The framework combines simulated precipitation, temperature, snow water equivalent (SWE), snowmelt, and streamflow with seasonal information in a rule‐based decision tree. Applied to 743 drought events across 22 sub‐basins over 1992–2023, the classification identifies distinct drought types with different duration, intensity, severity, and seasonal signatures. Composite droughts are the most frequent (26.8%), while warm and cold snow season pathways together account for 33.0% of events. Rain‐to‐snow droughts have the longest median duration and highest median severity, whereas warm snow season droughts show the highest median intensity. Sensitivity analyses show that the broad classification structure is retained across alternative design choices, although some decision parameters exert a strong control on class allocation and require local calibration. Hydro‐meteorological anomalies also provide season‐ and lead‐time‐dependent information on subsequent drought occurrence: spring SWE deficits and autumn precipitation deficits (mostly in October) were linked with the larger increase in drought probability. Our proposed framework provides a transparent basis for characterizing and tracking distinct drought‐onset pathways in mountain catchments and for informing process‐based drought monitoring.

articles.title: When GRACE Measures More Than Water: Geomorphic Mass Redistribution in Terrestrial Water Storage Trends
articles.titleEn: When GRACE Measures More Than Water: Geomorphic Mass Redistribution in Terrestrial Water Storage Trends
articles.abstract: The Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment and its Follow‐On missions (GRACE/GRACE‐FO) provide indirect estimates of regional‐scale water storage changes, albeit at a coarse resolution (∼300 km). Interpreting GRACE‐derived trends in geomorphically complex settings presents additional challenges. High rates of soil erosion, sediment transport, and deposition can affect gravity signals when they produce net mass export, accumulation, or source‐sink redistribution at GRACE‐relevant scales. Geomorphic correction of the GRACE signal is meaningful in arid regions, where sediment dynamics are active and terrestrial water storage variation is dominated by groundwater overdraft. In temperate and tropical climates, geomorphic mass redistribution becomes negligible as terrestrial water storage changes are much larger. Downscaled GRACE‐FO products may misrepresent groundwater storage changes if they are not grounded in a robust hydrogeological conceptualization. In this commentary, we discuss how sediment dynamics may affect hydrological GRACE‐based assessments using examples from arid source‐to‐sink sediment corridors. These cases illustrate that sediment transport models and hydrogeological conceptual models are essential tools for improving the interpretation of GRACE‐derived trends in hyper‐arid climates and catchments with accelerated erosion.

articles.title: Drought, Household Water Access, and Child Undernutrition: Evidence From Kenya
articles.titleEn: Drought, Household Water Access, and Child Undernutrition: Evidence From Kenya
articles.abstract: Climate change is putting immense strain on food and water resources, which can have dire health consequences. This is particularly concerning for young children, for whom undernutrition may have lasting social and health effects into adult life. Within the context of a severe long‐term drought in the Greater Horn of Africa between late 2020 and early 2023, we examined the relationship between exposure to the drought in Kenya, water access, and child nutritional status. We linked child‐ and household‐level data from the 2022 Kenyan Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) ( n = 16,632) with district‐level measures of drought exposure defined by the international disaster database (EM‐DAT) alongside measures of precipitation and temperature anomalies during the year preceding household surveys. Controlling for household demographics, we used logistic regression analyses to examine the relationship between drought, temperature, precipitation, water access, and three indicators of undernutrition for children under five: underweight, wasted, and stunted. Households who were exposed to the drought had lower odds of at least basic water access. Further, children exposed to the drought had higher odds of being wasted. Sensitivity analyses show consistent results, that increased temperature (both continuous measures and the top quintile of anomalies) was associated with higher odds of a child being wasted. Overall, the historic drought was associated with children's prevalence of undernutrition, highlighting the role of increased temperature. There is a need for future longitudinal research to explore the role of water access in mediating drought effects or improving drought recovery.

articles.title: Systematic Discrepancies Should Be Addressed Before Effective Parameter Learning: Insights From Soil Moisture Simulations Using Differentiable Process‐Based Models
articles.titleEn: Systematic Discrepancies Should Be Addressed Before Effective Parameter Learning: Insights From Soil Moisture Simulations Using Differentiable Process‐Based Models
articles.abstract: Differentiable hydrologic models combining neural networks with process‐based backbones—fully implemented or approximated by surrogate models—offer highly competitive accuracy and improved interpretability compared to either model type used alone. However, the impacts of surrogate model fidelity (accurate sensitivity of relationships compared to the original model) and systematic discrepancies between models and observations on parameter learning effectiveness remain underexplored. This study evaluates optimization performance of the differentiable HBV model ( δ HBV) and its surrogate variants in simulating soil moisture across the contiguous United States. Results show that high‐fidelity surrogate models can support effective differentiable parameter learning once systematic discrepancies are addressed. In contrast, unresolved systematic discrepancies degrade optimization performance, with particularly severe deterioration when low‐fidelity surrogates are used. These findings provide one possible explanation for the modest improvements reported in recent surrogate‐based differentiable parameter learning (dPL) applications. Linear correction partially mitigates these systematic discrepancies, improves optimization performance, and reduces compensatory parameter adjustment, although it does not resolve the underlying model–observation mismatch. Structural refinement remains a physically grounded long‐term direction, while pragmatic correction modules can provide useful partial mitigation when such refinement is not yet available. In addition, fully implementing differentiable process‐based models or using a rigorously trained surrogate can improve gradient fidelity and reduce amplified deterioration associated with surrogate infidelity.

articles.title: Contactless River Discharge From Unoccupied Aerial Systems Hydrometry: A Multi‐River Evaluation Across a Wide Range of Near‐Natural Cross‐Sectional Conditions
articles.titleEn: Contactless River Discharge From Unoccupied Aerial Systems Hydrometry: A Multi‐River Evaluation Across a Wide Range of Near‐Natural Cross‐Sectional Conditions
articles.abstract: Discharge is a fundamental hydrological variable, yet often unavailable under hard‐to‐access or critical conditions, hindering understanding of ungauged catchment hydrology. Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UAS) offer promising contactless approaches for monitoring inland waters under such conditions. Numerous studies have assessed UAS discharge estimation, but few have focused on evaluating fully contactless approaches across diverse river conditions. To address this gap, we present a UAS‐based framework for estimating discharge using contactless measurements of water surface velocity, water surface elevation, water surface slope and river bathymetry, supplemented by satellite observations and external DEMs where needed. Four surface‐to‐bulk velocity conversion methods: 0.85 coefficient, log law, power law and entropy method were applied. UAS discharge estimation accuracy was benchmarked at 46 cross‐sections across four river systems with gauge records. We quantified uncertainty propagation from each input variable, assessed their relative contributions, and performed an error propagation experiment to simulate high‐bias measurement scenarios. To identify factors controlling performance, we calculated correlations between discharge error, uncertainty metrics, and cross‐sectional properties. Across most cross‐sections, at least one method achieved discharge error less than 30%, though no single method consistently outperformed the others. The 0.85 method was robust with respect to input uncertainty, with performance patterns across methods linked to morphology: 0.85 and entropy methods performed generally better at larger rivers, while high water surface slopes reduced the accuracy of the log law and power law methods. Correlation analysis revealed that surface velocity uncertainty dominated discharge uncertainty in deep rivers, whereas water surface elevation was more influential in shallow ones.

UAS discharge estimation accuracy was benchmarked at 46 cross‐sections across four river systems with gauge records. We quantified uncertainty propagation from each input variable, assessed their relative contributions, and performed an error propagation experiment to simulate high‐bias measurement scenarios. To identify factors controlling performance, we calculated correlations between discharge error, uncertainty metrics, and cross‐sectional properties. Across most cross‐sections, at least one method achieved discharge error less than 30%, though no single method consistently outperformed the others. The 0.85 method was robust with respect to input uncertainty, with performance patterns across methods linked to morphology: 0.85 and entropy methods performed generally better at larger rivers, while high water surface slopes reduced the accuracy of the log law and power law methods. articles.title: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
articles.titleEn: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
articles.abstract: Extreme glacier melt events accelerate mass loss, increase glacier instability, and temporarily increase downstream runoff, potentially alleviating drought conditions. Yet the glacier energy–mass balance in the Geladandong region – a headwater region of the Yangtze River (China's longest river) and one of the source regions feeding Siling Co (Tibet's largest lake) – and its connection to the unprecedented 2022 summer melt remain insufficiently quantified. To address this gap, we integrated in-situ mass balance observations and glacio-meteorological data from a 5700 m monitoring site with an energy-mass balance model and applied a novel dual-threshold framework (based on mean and standard deviation) to identify extreme mass loss/melt events in short-term glacier mass balance records. Our novel methodology identified 2021/22 as a period of extreme mass loss and melt intensity, with melt during the 2022 summer heatwave reaching unprecedented extremes. These heatwaves caused an increase in melt amount of 317.8 mm w.e., amounting to 1.66 and 1.69 times the values recorded for the same period in 2019/20 and 2020/21, respectively. This extreme melt was driven by energy balance anomalies over the glacier surface. In terms of net contributions to the +28.2 W m −2 melt energy anomaly during the three identified heatwave windows, enhanced sensible heat flux was the largest term (+17.0 W m −2 ; 60.3 %), followed by increased net longwave radiation (+14.0 W m −2 ; 49.7 %) and increased net shortwave radiation (+5.1 W m −2 ; 18.1 %) associated with reduced albedo, with negative contributions from latent heat flux and subsurface heat flux. Such anomalies were driven by large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns, specifically the eastward extension and northward displacement of the South Asian High (SAH), together with near-neutral mid-latitude westerlies. This study advances the understanding of glacier mass balance responses to extreme weather and climate events on the central Tibetan Plateau.

articles.title: PLSTM-Reg v1.0: a regional physics-encoded LSTM model for simulating reservoir operations without site-specific training
articles.titleEn: PLSTM-Reg v1.0: a regional physics-encoded LSTM model for simulating reservoir operations without site-specific training
articles.abstract: Representing reservoir operations in large-scale hydrological models remains difficult due to complex release decisions and scarce operational records. Here, we develop PLSTM-Reg v1.0, a regional physics-encoded deep learning framework that explicitly enforces mass balance and operational constraints to simulate reservoir operations across diverse systems. The framework is evaluated using 256 representative reservoirs across the Contiguous United States, focusing on three core capabilities: temporal generalization to unseen periods, spatial transfer to unseen reservoirs, and historical data reconstruction in data-scarce reservoirs. Under temporal testing, the regional model improves 1 d-ahead release forecasts from a median Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of 0.83 to 0.96 relative to local counterparts (i.e., models trained exclusively on site-specific records), and reduces poorly simulated cases (KGE 0.5) increases from 56.6 % to 89.8 % for release and 14.4 % to 61.7 % for storage. In historical storage reconstruction, incorporating monthly satellite-derived surface area as a proxy for missing ground-based records enables reconstruction accuracy comparable to local models. These results demonstrate that cross-reservoir deep learning combined with physical knowledge provides a scalable scheme for representing human water management within large-scale hydrological and land surface models.

articles.title: Quantifying charger-related uncertainty in electrical mobility analysis of aerosols with MPSS-UQ 1.0
articles.titleEn: Quantifying charger-related uncertainty in electrical mobility analysis of aerosols with MPSS-UQ 1.0
articles.abstract: Charging probability is the greatest source of uncertainty in electrical mobility-based measurements of aerosol size distributions, but its influence on the results is rarely quantified and reported. In bipolar charging, the charge distribution is almost universally modeled using the Wiedensohler approximation, although it has been shown to deviate significantly from the true charge distribution under many measurement conditions. The charge distribution depends, among other factors, on the mobilities of the charger ions, which are typically not precisely known. Ignoring this uncertainty can lead to biased size distribution estimates and severe underestimation of their uncertainty. In this work, we quantify the uncertainty that imprecisely known charger ion mobilities introduce into the charged particle fractions, and then propagate this uncertainty into the estimates of the particle size distributions using a modular Bayesian approach, in which the ion mobilities are treated as nuisance parameters and marginalized over their plausible range. The inversion method, which is available as the open-source Python package MPSS-UQ, is implemented with particular emphasis on computational efficiency and tested with both synthetic and real mobility particle size spectrometer data. For a month-long field dataset, marginalizing over the uncertain ion mobilities widened the posterior credible intervals of the estimated size distributions on average by a factor of 2.4, with factors up to 10 in some size classes, compared to conditioning on fixed mobility values. The wider intervals provide a more realistic assessment of uncertainties in the inferred size distributions, and quantifying the structure of this uncertainty helps identify where improvements in the characterization of charger ion properties or in the measurement setup would be most effective.

articles.title: A hybrid physics–ML framework for integrating groundwater dynamics into land surface modeling: a ParFlow-based demonstration in headwater watersheds of the Pearl River Basin, China
articles.titleEn: A hybrid physics–ML framework for integrating groundwater dynamics into land surface modeling: a ParFlow-based demonstration in headwater watersheds of the Pearl River Basin, China
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional groundwater dynamics play a critical role in regulating land–atmosphere interactions, yet resolving three-dimensional subsurface flow processes at large scales remains computationally prohibitive. Here we present a hybrid coupling framework that enables the integration of three-dimensional groundwater processes into land surface modeling at substantially reduced computational cost. The framework replaces the physics-based groundwater solver with a deep learning surrogate while preserving the original coupling interface, providing a practical pathway for incorporating groundwater dynamics into Earth system simulations. A key feature of the framework is an error-control strategy based on a free-drainage lower bound, which approximates the treatment of subsurface processes in conventional land surface models where groundwater feedback is largely neglected. The hybrid solution is considered acceptable when its deviation remains below the free-drainage bound and, when specified, a user-defined threshold, allowing the fidelity criterion to be tailored to specific applications. The framework is demonstrated over three headwater watersheds covering approximately 34 000 km 2 in the Pearl River Basin, China, using the coupled CoLM/ParFlow model as the physics-based reference. The hybrid system achieves an 18.24× speedup while maintaining strong agreement with the physics-based reference. Over the 8040 h evaluation period (hours 721–8760 of water year 2021), the median water table depth error is within 0.5 m and the domain-averaged latent heat flux reaches a Kling–Gupta efficiency of 0.959. This study demonstrates the feasibility of hybrid surrogate–physics coupling for representing groundwater processes and provides a flexible foundation for multi-timescale, on-demand simulations. Although the trained surrogate is specific to the present study domain, the framework may be extended to other hydroclimatic settings through domain-specific retraining or fine-tuning and integrated into Earth system modeling frameworks.

articles.title: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
articles.titleEn: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
articles.abstract: Internal climate variability (ICV) represents the intrinsic fluctuations within the climate system. Understanding how ICV varies across regions, seasons, and climatic conditions is crucial for detecting externally forced climate change and assessing future climate risks. It can also provide a useful benchmark for assessing climate model performance and the emergence of anthropogenically forced climate change. This study aims to compare ICV estimates obtained using different methods and data types. We focus on seasonal mean near-surface air temperature over Europe, utilizing data from 15 CMIP6 models, a 100-member MPI-ESM large ensemble, and three observational datasets. The ICV estimates are based on pre-industrial control simulations (Pidata), the Hawkins and Sutton (2009) residual-based method (HS09), regression-based removal of external forcings, and a single-model large-ensemble framework. The magnitude of ICV estimates generally decreases from northeastern to southwestern Europe on both annual and seasonal timescales, except during JJA, when the highest estimates shift southward. The highest ICV estimates are observed in DJF and the lowest at the annual timescale. Among all the methods, Pidata generally yields the highest ICV estimates across all seasonal and annual timescales, except during JJA. Based on the HS09 method, the similarity between the model-based estimates and the observations is most pronounced during DJF and at the annual timescale. However, this similarity is weaker when the regression-based method is applied, with the model-based estimates generally exceeding the observation-based ones. The projected changes in ICV show a tendency for reduced (enhanced) values in DJF (JJA). Although a north-south contrast emerges in other seasons, with declining (increasing) ICV in northern (southern) Europe, the overall spatial pattern indicates a reduction in projected ICV estimates across large parts of Europe, except during JJA.

articles.title: A new global dataset of photosynthesis parameters
articles.titleEn: A new global dataset of photosynthesis parameters
articles.abstract: Photosynthesis-irradiance and photosynthesis-depth experiments are two standard ways of experimentally quantifying primary production. These measurements have historically formed the backbone for the formulation of mathematical models of primary production and to this day remain an invaluable resource for model development and refinement. From such experiments information on photosynthesis parameters can be extracted, which allows for the quantification of the photosynthesis light dependence, essential in the calculation of primary production. To this day, such experiments remain the primary source of photosynthesis parameters, making such data invaluable for primary production modelling. In the literature, there have been several efforts to form global datasets of photosynthesis parameters, collected at various sites across the world oceans and seas. Here, we use a publicly available global dataset of in situ primary production profiles and construct a new database of photosynthesis parameters. We use an inverse modelling approach that is described in great details, along with the data requirements. For a forward model, we employ a fully solvable analytical model of the production profile, and we use the inverse model to compare it with the measured production profile, while constraining it with measured daily watercolumn production. Using this approach, we successfully recovered 3776 photosynthesis-irradiance parameters from the global oceans, which enabled a model versus data comparison for watercolumn production. The spatio-temporal distribution of the new dataset is presented and compared to existing datasets. Finally, the new photosynthesis parameters dataset is provided publicly, along with metadata needed for the implementation in primary production models. The dataset can be accessed via the Zenodo repository at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17973417 (Kovač et al., 2025).

articles.title: A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
articles.titleEn: A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
articles.abstract: Active layer thickness (ALT) is a key indicator of permafrost change, with important implications for soil hydrothermal conditions, carbon feedbacks, ecosystem processes, and cold-region infrastructure. However, hemispheric-scale ALT mapping remains challenging because field observations are sparse and unevenly distributed, while thaw depth is controlled by complex and nonlinear environmental interactions. Here, we developed a LightGBM–XGBoost ensemble framework to reconstruct annual ALT on a 1 km grid across the Northern Hemisphere permafrost region from 2000 to 2024. Spatial block cross-validation yielded an R 2 of 0.720 and an RMSE of 39.47 cm, while complementary leave-one-site-out cross-validation achieved an R 2 of 0.780 and an RMSE of 34.98 cm. Temporally blocked validation using all withheld observations from 2021–2024 achieved an R 2 of 0.693 and an RMSE of 26.36 cm, improving to an R 2 of 0.826 and an RMSE of 19.74 cm when evaluation was restricted to previously observed sites. Across 60 long-term monitoring sites, the observed and reconstructed mean ALT series showed close temporal agreement ( r =0.954), although site-specific year-to-year variability was substantially smoothed, with predicted detrended variability reaching only about 64 % of the observed amplitude. The reconstructed ALT showed an overall long-term increase during 2000–2024, together with pronounced geographic and ecological heterogeneity. Annual area-of-applicability layers and site-resampling uncertainty estimates are provided to characterize environmental extrapolation and sensitivity to monitoring-network composition. Validation performance was not uniform across environmental and ALT conditions, with substantially larger errors for deep-thaw conditions and sparsely represented settings. The dataset is therefore most suitable for regional- to hemispheric-scale analyses of spatial ALT patterns and long-term permafrost change, while local-scale variability, deep-thaw conditions, and extrapolated areas should be interpreted with caution. The dataset is archived and freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23227837 (Wei and Chen, 2026).

articles.title: The MAESTRO turbulence dataset derived from the SAFIRE ATR42 aircraft
articles.titleEn: The MAESTRO turbulence dataset derived from the SAFIRE ATR42 aircraft
articles.abstract: The MAESTRO airborne field campaign took place between 10 August and 10 September 2024 over the North Atlantic tropical ocean near the Cabo Verde Islands. Its goal was to investigate the processes that control the mesoscale organization of clouds with a payload of probes and sensors, as well as vertically and horizontally-pointing radars and lidars. A particular attention was given to the role of coherent structures in the boundary layer. This focus motivated the acquisition of high-resolution measurements of temperature and water vapor to capture turbulence dynamics in the subcloud layer. To achieve this, six hygrometers and four temperature sensors were deployed, including a new fast-rate hygrometer called FAST-WAVE. This article describes the turbulence dataset, prepared on the basis of these measurements. It consists of 25 Hz segmented time series of calibrated water vapor mixing ratio, temperature, and three-dimensional wind taken with an air speed of approximately 100 m s −1 , relative to the aircraft, their corresponding fluctuations, as well as statistical moments, covariance, and integral length scales. In total, 40 h of stabilized legs data were gathered in a wide range of mesoscale contexts and local cloud conditions, with nearly 13 h consisting of high-quality boundary-layer samples. This paper describes the methodological choices required to obtain the dataset, including calibrations, and corrections applied to the original measurements. The collection of NetCDF files composing this dataset is publicly available on the AERIS website (https://doi.org/10.25326/812#v7.0, Jaffeux and Lothon, 2025; see also https://maestro.aeris-data.fr/overview/, last access: 9 June 2026).

articles.title: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
articles.titleEn: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
articles.abstract: Nitrogen (N) input is expected to intensify phosphorus (P) limitation in tropical and subtropical forests. However, how soil and microbial processes mobilize P from poorly available pools to sustain soil P bioavailability remains unclear. We conducted a nine‐year experiment with low (20 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) and high (80 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) N addition treatments in a subtropical Moso bamboo ( Phyllostachys edulis ) plantation. We quantified soil P fractions, P‐cycling functional genes, phosphatase activity, P sorption capacity (PSC), iron and aluminum oxides, and plant properties throughout the experiment. Our results reveal three distinct stages in the regulation of soil bioavailable P with prolonged N addition. Phase I: N addition reduces P bioavailability, and labile organic P decomposition becomes the main source of bioavailable P, associated with increased phosphatase activity. Phase II: when labile organic P becomes insufficient to meet P demand, bioavailable P is replenished through the depletion of moderately labile organic P; this is related to decreased PSC and enhanced acid phosphomonoesterases activity. Phase III: stable organic P decreases significantly, jointly sustaining bioavailable P with the depletion of other organic P fractions, alongside a further decrease in PSC and enriched microbial organic acid‐ and phosphatase‐related genes. This study uncovers a novel “three‐phased P supply” model revealed through long‐term observations. These mechanistic insights reveal the pathways of soil P mobilization under continuous N input in a subtropical forest and establish a framework for predicting the buffering capacity of soil P pools in P‐limited ecosystems under global change scenarios.

articles.title: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
articles.titleEn: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
articles.abstract: Permafrost regions store vast quantities of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the future trajectories of functionally distinct SOC fractions across soil depths remain poorly constrained. Integrating depth‐explicit soil fractionation data from 104 sites across the Tibetan permafrost region with a process‐based SOC model, we project century‐scale dynamics of particulate (POC) and mineral‐associated organic carbon (MAOC) under three emission scenarios. We show that MAOC currently comprises 56.5% of regional total SOC stock and remains far from saturation throughout the profile. Consistent with this large stabilization capacity, total SOC was projected to increase over the 21st century under all scenarios, with the largest gains under SSP5‐8.5. However, this positive net gain masked a significant restructuring of SOC fractions. MAOC accumulated across all depths and scenarios, and heavy POC remained comparatively buffered, whereas light POC declined under SSP5‐8.5. The strongest relative light POC losses occurred in the 10–30 cm layers, where warming‐driven decomposition remained strong while plant‐C input compensation weakened. These divergent trajectories indicate a shift toward a “carbon‐rich yet energy‐poor” state, where mineral‐bound carbon increases while the labile particulate pool supporting microbial activity is depleted. Our findings reveal SOC vulnerability in permafrost region is governed by both fraction identity and soil depth, and that net SOC gains can conceal the loss of metabolically active carbon. Incorporating measurable, depth‐resolved SOC fractions into Earth system models is therefore essential for constraining permafrost–climate feedbacks.

articles.title: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
articles.titleEn: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
articles.abstract: Land‐use changes induced by human activities usually accelerate soil erosion, leading to losses of soil organic matter (SOM). The mechanisms by which cultivation‐associated degradation affects SOM composition via changes of content and quality of particulate (POM), mineral‐associated (MAOM), dissolved organic matter (DOM), and microbial biomass are not elucidated. We investigated the C:N stoichiometry of these fractions, and erosion (using 137 Cs activity) along a chronosequence of cultivation‐associated degradation (0–114 years) in Mollisols. Two‐pool and Bayesian three‐source mixing models estimated contributions of microbial biomass, DOM, and POM to MAOM to the total SOM. Erosion intensity ranged locally from 440 to 4800 t km −2 year −1 , resulting in cumulative soil losses of 11,000 to 320,000 t km −2 over 114 years of cultivation. As cultivation duration and eroded amounts increased, the C/N ratios of POM, MAOM, and DOM declined owing to (i) the faster loss of C than N, (ii) a decrease in C/N with soil depth involved in tillage horizon, and (iii) N input by fertilization. These higher C than N losses reflect that erosion is not the sole process leading to the decline of C stocks, but intensive cultivation also accelerates organic matter mineralization and CO 2 release to the atmosphere. As the C/N ratios of POM and MAOM declined but microbial C/N increased, the estimated contribution of microbial inputs to MAOM increased from 6% to 32%. The Bayesian model partitioned MAOM sources into DOM (8%), microbial (11%), and POM (81%), reinforcing that POM dominates MAOM formation in croplands. Cultivation‐associated degradation led to SOC losses by reducing POM‐C/N and MAOM‐C/N ratios, while erosion strongly accelerated these effects. Furthermore, cultivation‐associated degradation is also based on the limited inputs of organic C as the precursors for MAOM formation by depleting POM. These results from a > 100‐year chronosequence indicate that cultivation‐induced degradation reduces SOM content, while also shifting the MAOM composition progressively towards a greater contribution of microbial C.

articles.title: CO 2 fertilization to climate limitation: shifting drivers in a dryland forest
articles.titleEn: CO 2 fertilization to climate limitation: shifting drivers in a dryland forest
articles.abstract: Dryland forests represent a significant but uncertain component of the terrestrial carbon sink, where rising CO 2 and intensifying drought and heat stress exert opposing controls on carbon and water fluxes. Using ED2.2-hydraulics calibrated against 21 years of flux tower and inventory data from Yatir Forest, an arid pine plantation in Israel, we simulated carbon fluxes, biomass dynamics, and water-use efficiency under current climate and high-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) through 2100 using five general circulation models. CO 2 fertilization initially enhanced productivity and biomass accumulation despite periodic drought, with the strongest response under SSP3-7.0. Under SSP5-8.5, compound heat and drought stress suppressed productivity below SSP3-7.0 levels despite higher CO 2 concentrations, triggering stand collapse in two projections and eliminating approximately 40 % of accumulated biomass. Driver decomposition showed that forest responses shifted from CO 2 -dominated to interaction-dominated by late century, with compound heat and drought stress explaining 39 %–66 % of the relative importance of all drivers by late century. Apparent biomass gains under severe scenarios reflected accumulation in fewer, larger surviving individuals as stand density declined, masking structural deterioration in aggregate metrics. Functional decline (productivity, water-use efficiency) preceded structural changes by 7–37 years depending on scenario, providing an early warning window before visible deterioration. These results show that CO 2 fertilization benefits cannot compensate for the compound climate extremes that accompany high emissions, and that functional indicators must be monitored alongside structural metrics to detect forest vulnerability in dryland afforestation systems.

articles.title: Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
articles.titleEn: Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
articles.abstract: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospheric CO 2 forcing using the Model for Interdisciplinary Research on Climate, Earth System version 2 for Long-term simulations (MIROC-ES2L) Earth system model driven by extended Shared Socio-economic Pathway (SSP) scenarios through to the year 2500. Ocean–atmosphere p CO 2 disequilibrium exhibits strong scenario dependence. Under the low-emission scenario SSP1–2.6, oceanic CO 2 undersaturation gradually weakens and approaches near equilibrium by 2100. By contrast, under the high-emission scenario SSP5–8.5, rapid increase in atmospheric p CO 2 results in increasing undersaturation of CO 2 in the ocean over the 21st century. Thereafter, surface-ocean CO 2 supersaturation progressively expand into the equatorial and subtropical oceans between the mid–23rd and late 25th century. The Southern Ocean remains persistently undersaturated throughout the simulations, consistent with sustained influence from deep waters that are weakly affected by anthropogenic perturbations. Under SSP5–8.5, oceanic CO 2 uptake continues to increase until the late 21st century. Thereafter, it gradually weakens as surface-ocean p CO 2 approaches atmospheric levels, whereas the Southern Ocean remains a persistent carbon sink throughout the simulation. Across all scenarios, early oceanic p CO 2 changes are primarily driven by increases in dissolved inorganic carbon, whereas alkalinity becomes an increasingly important control from the mid–22nd century onward under SSP5–8.5. A progressive decline in the oceanic CO 2 buffering capacity, driven by cumulative CO 2 uptake, increases the sensitivity of surface-ocean p CO 2 to additional carbon uptake. The buffering capacity approaches its effective minimum levels by the late 22nd century. In parallel, enhanced upper-ocean stratification and a slowdown of the deep overturning circulation reduce the upward transport of high alkalinity waters to the surface. This results in a decline in surface-ocean alkalinity that further enhances the influence of alkalinity on surface-ocean p CO 2 during this period. Marine biological productivity and export vary significantly as a function of atmospheric CO 2 trajectory. It increases under low-emission scenarios but declines under sustained high-emission scenarios. The transition between the two behaviors occurs when pCO2atm reaches approximately 3 times the preindustrial level and is closely associated with the weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and the resulting nutrient redistribution. Thermal stress and nutrient limitation persist in regions such as the Arctic Ocean until the late 25th century even under SSP1–2.6, indicating a centennial-scale lagged response of marine ecosystems to atmospheric CO 2 forcing. In the surface ocean, marine ecosystem stress (integrating thermal and biogeochemical stressors) continues to intensify through the late 22nd century under SSP5–8.5, despite the stabilization of atmospheric p CO 2 , highlighting the long memory and limited reversibility of oceanic ecosystem stress.

articles.title: Technical note: a Recognition-assisted Camera for Automated Microscopy (RaCAM)
articles.titleEn: Technical note: a Recognition-assisted Camera for Automated Microscopy (RaCAM)
articles.abstract: Automated microscopy workflows, including image acquisition, processing, and recognition using artificial intelligence (AI), are getting a growing interest from the scientific community in biogeosciences, as more and more research institutes are actively working on building datasets of images to train artificial convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to identify microscopic objects. Here, we present a new, affordable, AI-assisted, and open-source Raspberry Pi-powered camera that can fit any microscope equipped with a regular C-mount (or CS-mount) camera thread. This camera is the first fully self-contained camera equipped with an integrated Single-Board Computer (Raspberry Pi 5) and high-resolution camera sensor (12.3 mp), attached together using a 3D-printable adaptor. Using two new open-source workflows written using the Python language and freely downloadable too, the camera is capable of performing automated microscopy using either an automated image segmentation workflow (RaCAM IS software, including image acquisition, automated image processing, and object recognition using trained ResNet50 CNN models) or an object detection workflow (RaCAM OD software, including image acquisition and automated still image/live stream object detection using YOLO models). The camera is also adapted to on-field tasks such as core description, biostratigraphy or even palaeoenvironmental reconstructions based on microfossils census data or morphometry, as it can operate without the need for a spare computer and run directly on a power bank. Finally, since the automated microscopy workflows rely on images directly captured by the camera, applications can also be extended outside of the microscopy and micropaleontology research fields as any picture acquired with this device can virtually be processed.
